transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Janine Herbst.
California voters have rejected a ballot measure that would have imposed a one-time 5 percent
tax on the personal assets of billionaires, according to a call by the Associated Press.
Proposition 40 would have directed most of that tax revenue to health care.
After meeting with the Prime Minister of Qatar in Washington today, President Trump held
an impromptu press conference from the White House saying he's standing by Defense Secretary
Pete Hegseth, even in the face of an impeachment effort filed today by outgoing Republican
Congressman Thomas Massie.
Trump was apparently speaking about Iran and Venezuela, which was the object of a military
operation to seize its oil.
Mississippi's U.S. Senate race still hasn't been called but is nearing the deadline for
ballots to be accepted.
Democrat Scott Colom currently leads the race against Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith
by about 2,500 votes.
Kristin Kaler of Mississippi Public Broadcasting has more.
The race still hasn't been called, but about 97 percent of ballots have now been counted.
In Hines County, which includes parts of Metro Jackson, Election Commissioner Kadada Brown
says she wants people to understand accuracy is more important than speed.
The integrity of this matter is more important than anything, so that's why I ask everyone
to be patient and give us a little grace.
Mail-in and affidavit ballots, also known as provisional ballots, are still being counted.
The deadline for those to be accepted is Tuesday.
Counties have until Friday to certify complete results.
The Mississippi Secretary of State's office has not responded to requests for updated information
on the ballot count.
For NPR News, I'm Kristin Kaler in Jackson, Mississippi.
The man accused of killing conservative activist Charlie Kirk on a Utah college campus now
has a trial date.
In June 21st, 2028, that's when jury selection will begin in Tyler Robinson's trial, Fourth District Judge Tony Graff ruled.
This trial setting and case management order's intent is to ensure that the constitutional
rights of Mr. Robinson and Mrs. Kirk are upheld at every junction.
Kirk's widow, Erica, requested a speedy trial several times.
In court, her attorney Jeffrey Nyman told Judge Graff that the trial date he set was
not appropriate.
A trial in the summer of 2028, three years after Charlie's assassination, does not feel
very speedy to the Kirk family.
Robinson has pleaded not guilty to seven charges, including aggravated murder, which can carry
the death penalty.
For NPR News, I'm Hugo Ricardo Bell in Provo, Utah.
This is NPR News.
A piece of civil rights history is set to be auctioned off in January.
That's when a rough draft of Martin Luther King, Jr.'s famous "I Have a Dream" speech
goes up for sale by Christie's auction house.
The New York Times says this version, handwritten the night before his speech in a hotel room
on a yellow pad and full of crossed-out passages, was found in a desk drawer of his former aide,
Edward T. Clayton.
And like the final typed draft, this one doesn't include his famous line "I Have a Dream."
King improvised that line as he delivered his message on the steps of the Lincoln Memorial
in Washington, D.C. in August of 1963.
Dinosaur bones are found pretty often.
A new study claims to have found something exceedingly rare, though, dinosaur blood.
And Piers Nate Rott has more.
To be clear, we're not talking about a vial of dinosaur blood, nor even a trail of dried
dino blood.
Instead, researchers say they found chemical traces of red blood cells and tiny mineralized
structures that look like red blood cells in a 115 million-year-old bone.
The study, published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, claims to
be the most compelling evidence yet of dinosaur blood.
Other researchers who are not involved in the new study agree that the evidence is intriguing.
And they're not ready to say these structures are actually red blood cells.
Nate Rott, NPR News.
U.S. futures contracts are trading in mixed territory.
Dow futures up about 142 points.
NASDAQ futures down 20 points.
This is NPR.
This message comes from Lisa and their lineup of beautifully crafted mattresses tailored
to how you sleep.
Go to LEESA.com for up to 25% off mattresses, plus get an extra $50 off with a promo code
NPR.

topics.text: California voters reject Proposition 40, a one-time 5 percent tax on billionaires' personal assets
Trump says he stands by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth amid impeachment effort by Thomas Massie
Mississippi Senate race between Scott Colom and Cindy Hyde-Smith still uncalled, with mail ballots still counting
Judge sets June 2028 trial date for Tyler Robinson, accused of killing Charlie Kirk
Christie's to auction handwritten rough draft of Martin Luther King Jr.'s 'I Have a Dream' speech in January
Study claims chemical traces of dinosaur red blood cells found in 115-million-year-old bone
U.S. stock futures trade mixed, Dow up and Nasdaq down in early trading
